title: Deep learning identifies and counts wild animals in camera-trap photos

crossref.container: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

open_copies.title_found: Automatically identifying, counting, and describing wild animals in camera-trap images with deep learning
passages: We train deep convolutional neural networks to identify, count, and describe the behaviors of 48 species in the 3.2 million-image Snapshot Serengeti dataset.

For example, we show deep learning can automate animal identification for 99.3% of the 3.2 million-image Snapshot Serengeti dataset while performing at the same 96.6% accuracy of crowdsourced teams of human volunteers.

Keywords: deep learning, deep neural networks, artificial intelligence, camera-trap images, wildlife ecologyAbstract Having accurate, detailed, and up-to-date information about the location and behavior of animals in the wild would improve our ability to study and conserve ecosystems.
Our deep neural networks automatically identify animals with >93.8% accuracy, and we expect that number to improve rapidly in years to come.
Animal identification in low quality camera-trap images using very deep convolutional neural networks and confidence thresholds; pp.
Here, we demonstrate that a cutting-edge type of artificial intelligence called deep neural networks can automatically extract such invaluable information.

open_copies.title_found: Automatically identifying, counting, and describing wild animals in camera-trap images with deep learning
passages: We train deep convolutional neural networks to identify, count, and describe the behaviors of 48 species in the 3.2-million-image Snapshot Serengeti dataset.
Our deep neural networks automatically identify animals with over 93.8% accuracy, and we expect that number to improve rapidly in years to come.
Those efficiency gains immediately highlight the importance of using deep neural networks to automate data extraction from camera-trap images.
We demonstrate that such information can be automatically extracted by deep learning, a cutting-edge type of artificial intelligence.
Having accurate, detailed, and up-to-date information about the location and behavior of animals in the wild would revolutionize our ability to study and conserve ecosystems.
We investigate the ability to automatically, accurately, and inexpensively collect such data, which could transform many fields of biology, ecology, and zoology into "big data" sciences.
